sources.entry: CrossMacro - A cross-platform macro recorder, player, editor, and text expansion tool.

summary.one_liner: CrossMacro is a free, open-source mouse and keyboard macro recorder, player, and visual editor for Linux, Windows, and macOS, with text expansion and automation triggers.
summary.what_it_does: Records mouse movements, clicks, scrolling, and keyboard events, then saves them as reusable .macro files that can be replayed with adjustable speed, countdowns, repeat counts, and delays, and paused or resumed during playback. A visual editor lets users reorder or remove recorded steps and add text, delays, clipboard and window actions, variables, loops, and conditions, including waits for colors, images, or windows. Macros can be launched by global keyboard or mouse shortcuts, run once, at intervals, or on daily or weekly schedules, or triggered when the focused window's class, title, or process name matches a rule. Text expansion turns abbreviations into longer text, and named profiles keep macro libraries, shortcuts, schedules, and settings separate. A CLI and a local MCP server share the same automation engine, with the CLI offering structured JSON output.
use_cases: Record and replay repetitive data entry or form filling
Expand abbreviations into standard email addresses or replies
Automate recurring desktop tasks on a schedule or hotkey
Run UI checks that wait for a color, image, or window
Trigger macros when a specific window is focused
Script desktop actions from the command line with JSON output
Give a local AI agent controlled desktop automation via MCP
how_to_run: Download an installer from the project's download guide (Flathub, DEB, RPM, AUR, AppImage, NixOS on Linux; Microsoft Store, winget, or portable EXE on Windows; DMG on macOS)
Complete the platform setup guide (permissions, group changes, or Gatekeeper steps)
Open CrossMacro, focus a text editor, press F8 to start recording, press F8 again to stop
Press F9 to replay the macro; F10 pauses or resumes playback
Save the macro from Files to reuse it
notable: Supports both Wayland and X11 on Linux, plus native Windows and macOS integrations
Shared automation engine across the GUI, CLI, and a local MCP server, with a restricted mode for agents
Window-focus and workspace triggers that can also switch profiles on supported desktops
Visual step editor with variables, loops, conditions, and screen-aware waits
caveats: macOS DMGs are unsigned and not notarized, so Gatekeeper and privacy permissions must be set up manually
Setup and capabilities vary by platform and desktop session; automation needs an active desktop session and the GUI-less runtime is not a display-less server
GitHub MSIX files are unsigned advanced/test packages; normal Windows install should use Store, winget, or portable EXE
